clue.text: Social position of a virtuous person in church

indicators.note: in means the saintly pair of letters is placed inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ST, short for saint, is a virtuous person

explanation.surface: Asks where a good churchgoer stands socially among the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary class in a rigid social hierarchy fixes one's social position.

clue.text: Unattractive church short of members

parts.note: members are limbs, so lacking arms is short of members

explanation.surface: A dreary church lacking enough members in its congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking charm or appeal means plain and unappealing.

clue.text: Watertight vessel, starting off, got under way

indicators.note: in a down entry, got under means the trimmed vessel is placed below the way

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: starting off means the vessel loses its first letter

parts.note: a launch is a motorboat

explanation.surface: A tight boat began its voyage after shedding its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting off' drops the L of LAUNCH, leaving AUNCH; 'got under' puts it beneath ST in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch vessel is one that does not leak, an old nautical sense.

clue.text: Poem English youth leader's written about cricket side

indicators.note: written about means the letters are set around the cricket side
leader's picks the first letter of youth

parts.note: leg is the on side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A verse by an English youth captain on the cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful lyric poem, often a lament for the dead.

clue.text: Follow short composition's violin part

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a piece is a short musical or literary composition

explanation.surface: A violin section that comes after a short composition.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin, the tailpiece is the fitting at the bottom to which the strings are anchored.

clue.text: Wrapping it up, left without dope

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the letters go round the information
up in a down clue means the word it is read upwards

parts.note: taken as written
dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: Packaging it after leaving behind the drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IT to TI; with L added, TIL goes 'without' (outside) INFO: T + INFO + IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet used to cover food is a kind of packaging.

clue.text: Type of rock in use — go to mine it?

indicators.note: mining breaks up rock, so the letters are broken and reshaped

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should dig out a rock that is being used.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock formed from cooled magma, like granite, is one of the main kinds.

clue.text: Quiet person fiddling cash, but not a robber

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: not means the letter A is excluded from the word

parts.note: a launderer passes off illicit cash as legitimate

explanation.surface: A discreet embezzler who is no thief.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the fiddler is not a robber; 'not a' removes an A from LAUNDERER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pillages or loots is a thief.

clue.text: Involve small sibling in climbing tree

indicators.note: in means the sibling goes inside the tree
climbing in a down clue means the tree reads upwards

parts.note: the lime is a tree
bro is short for brother

explanation.surface: Get a little brother involved in going up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the tree upwards in this down entry, giving EMIL, and 'in' houses the sibling within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to entangle someone in a conflict, to drag them in.

clue.text: Crossing Atlantic state, gaze at lofty dwelling

indicators.note: Crossing means the gazing word straddles the state, which lies inside it

parts.note: to eye is to gaze at
RI is Rhode Island, on the Atlantic coast

explanation.surface: Travelling across the Atlantic, one stares at a high home.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built high on a crag is an elevated home.

clue.text: No man's prepared to host spirited king of Mycenae

indicators.note: to host means the rearranged letters take in another word, as a host takes in a guest
prepared means the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
game means plucky, spirited

explanation.surface: Nobody is ready to entertain a lively Greek king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the letters into AMNON; 'to host' places the spirited word after its first A. Agamemnon led the Greeks at Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the leader of the Greeks at Troy ruled Mycenae.

clue.text: Natural pigment from estuary identified by Cockney?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops his aitches, so the name loses its initial H as a Londoner would say it

parts.note: the Humber is an estuary in north-east England

explanation.surface: A Londoner names an earth colour after an estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is a large estuary in Yorkshire and Lincolnshire; Cockneys famously drop the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown earth used as a pigment by painters, from Umbria, is a natural colouring.

clue.text: Easy profit made by supplying bread for elderly painter

parts.note: bread is slang for money
taken as written
elderly means old
a painter is the rope at the bow of a boat used for tying up

explanation.surface: Cash paid to support an aged artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' looks like an artist but is a boat's mooring line.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means payment for very little effort, a gain obtained easily.

clue.text: Morally correct concerning racial study, omitting name

indicators.note: omitting means the letter for name is left out of the word

parts.note: ethnical is an older adjective meaning relating to ethnology, the study of races

explanation.surface: A view on racial studies that is morally right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical conduct conforms to accepted moral principles, so it is morally right.

clue.text: Designed a niche fit for a clan leader

indicators.note: Designed means the letters are shaped into a new pattern

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A recess built suitably for the head of a Highland clan.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a Scottish clan is its chief.

clue.text: Extra place by old city in South America

indicators.note: in means the city and place are set inside the South American letters

parts.note: US is America
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: An additional location beside an ancient city in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A surplus is an amount beyond what is needed, an excess.

clue.text: Brisk, with good reason, following latest odds

indicators.note: following means the reasoned word comes after the odds

parts.note: SP, the starting price, is the final odds before a race
rightly means justifiably, with good reason

explanation.surface: Quick, and justified, after the latest betting prices.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing the SP is the starting price, the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and energetic, full of vigour, is quick and spry.

clue.text: False argument occasioned work for clubs in division

indicators.note: for means one piece stands in place of another within the word

parts.note: a schism is a division or split, especially in a church
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A split in a group caused by labour in place of a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps: OP replaces the C in SCHISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plausible but fallacious line of reasoning is a deceptive argument.

clue.text: Joint cover provided in Asian and American city

parts.note: Patel is a very common South Asian surname, standing for an Asian
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Insurance for a joint offered in an Asian and American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint cover' sounds like a policy; it is the kneecap. Patel is a common Indian surname used for an Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is the bone protecting the knee joint.

clue.text: Scholars carrying headgear for Indian sage

indicators.note: carrying means the scholars hold the headgear between them

parts.note: two MAs, Masters of Arts, are scholars
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: Academics wearing hats for a wise man from India.
explanation.definitionFit: A title of reverence for a holy, wise person in India.

clue.text: Salt water finally crossed by sea king

indicators.note: crossed by means the sea word has a letter passing through it

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of water

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina's abbreviation, used for a monarch, here a king (Rex is R; ER also appears for Edward Rex)

explanation.surface: Salt water traversed by a king of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' in the surface is an adjective for water; it is the definition, an old sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, a seaman.

clue.text: Incense forced on audience in a London theatre?

indicators.note: on audience means the words are as heard by listeners

parts.note: myrrh is an incense resin, and made means forced, as in made him go

explanation.surface: Incense pushed onto spectators in a West End playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mermaid Theatre is in the City of London, at Blackfriars.
explanation.definitionFit: The playhouse at Puddle Dock, Blackfriars, opened in 1959.

clue.text: Lives with officer initially in no state for offensive

indicators.note: in means the lives and officer letters sit inside the other pair

parts.note: taken as written
ME is Maine
lives means is, as in exists

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of officer

explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant and smelly, disgusting, is repellent.

clue.text: Unlikely to win, no longer in control

definitions.meaning: a contender with no chance of victory
no longer managing or running things

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without a chance of success, and also no longer running an enterprise.

clue.text: Soldiers with little time for astronauts' course

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers
a bit is a short while

explanation.surface: Troops spend a short while on space training.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved path of a spacecraft round the earth is its flight path.

clue.text: Like the particular sound of a hooter?

definitions.text: Like the particular sound of a hooter?

parts.words: Like the particular sound of a hooter?
parts.note: a hooter is slang for the nose, so this describes speech coming through the nose

explanation.definitionFit: Speech that resonates through the nose is said to have that quality.

clue.text: Take part in tribal sacrifice in a wood

indicators.note: Take part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'in a wood' as the definition, but 'in' is a link word: the wood itself is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree.

clue.text: Convict previously shipped Ecstasy

definitions.meaning: a convict formerly sent overseas, to Australia, as punishment

explanation.definitionFit: To deport convicts to a penal colony was the old sentence; a rapture of joy is the other sense.

clue.text: Former militiamen give instruction to players

parts.note: to train is to give instruction
a band is a group of musical players

explanation.surface: Old soldiers teach musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained bands were companies of citizen soldiers in England in the 16th-17th centuries.

clue.text: Cautious general going by public transport

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A careful general rides the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary or suspicious means being careful.
